title: US Flight Delays and Cancellations in January 2024
text:
For this project I loaded all 547,271 US domestic flights from January 2024 into a MySQL database on AWS and answered the seven assignment questions with SQL. This page shows what I found. The queries and full results are on the SQL Questions page.
In January 2024, 20,389 flights (3.7%) were cancelled. Most of them came from two events: a week of winter storms in the middle of the month, and the grounding of the Boeing 737 MAX 9.

title: US Flight Delays and Cancellations in January 2024
text:
Cancellations by day


                            
                                            


Every cancelled flight has a reason code. Weather cancellations came in spikes. The worst day was January 15 with 2,962 cancellations, and January 12 to 16 alone had 46% of all cancellations in the month.
Carrier cancellations, the ones caused by the airline itself, look different. There were about 16 a day from January 1 to 5, then about 335 a day from January 6 to 27. On January 5 a door plug blew out of an Alaska Airlines 737 MAX 9 during a flight, and the FAA grounded these planes the next day. Alaska and United were the two US airlines flying this model. Alaska started flying them again on January 26 and United on January 27.

title: US Flight Delays and Cancellations in January 2024
text:
Cancellations by airline


                            
                                            


Alaska cancelled 17.6% of its flights and United 8.0%. Every other airline was under 6%, and Delta was the lowest at 0.6%. Alaska and United also had 6,895 of the 7,736 carrier cancellations (89%). The data has no aircraft type column, so I can’t connect a single flight to the grounding, but the airlines and the dates match.

title: US Flight Delays and Cancellations in January 2024
text:
Delays by airline


                            
                                            


Delays rank the airlines differently. American had the highest average departure delay at 25.5 minutes, but it cancelled only 1.6% of its flights. Alaska and United were in the middle at about 19 minutes. An airline can cancel few flights and still be late a lot, and the other way around.

title: US Flight Delays and Cancellations in January 2024
text:
Delays by time of day


                            
                                            


Delays build up during the day, probably because a late plane also makes its next flight late. Only 9.9% of flights scheduled between 6 and 7 a.m. left 15 or more minutes late. For flights scheduled between 7 and 8 p.m. it was 32.1%.

title: US Flight Delays and Cancellations in January 2024
text:
Small airports
The airport with the highest average departure delay (Problem 4) is North Central West Virginia airport (CKB) at 86 minutes. But CKB had only 15 departures in January, so a few very late flights decide its average. Some answers in Problem 5 have the same problem.

title: US Flight Delays and Cancellations in January 2024
text:
Data and method
The data is the Reporting Carrier On-Time Performance table from the Bureau of Transportation Statistics for January 2024, with one row per flight. I created the schema FAA on AWS RDS (MySQL) and the fact table al_perf, copied the CSV to an EC2 instance with scp, and loaded it with mysqlimport. The six lookup tables (airlines, airports, airport IDs, cancellation reasons, distance groups and weekdays) were loaded with the MySQL Workbench import wizard.
mysqlimport saves empty numbers as 0. A cancelled flight that never left the gate has an empty departure time and delay, so its delay becomes 0 after loading. For the delay questions I only use flights that have a departure time (DepTime <> '').
The charts are made with Python (pandas and Plotly) from the query results, and the site is built with Quarto.

title: SQL Questions
text: All queries run on the schema FAA, which has the fact table al_perf and the lookup tables. For the delay questions (1, 2, 4 and 5) I only use flights that have a departure time, because mysqlimport saved the empty delays of cancelled flights as 0.

title: SQL Questions
text:
Problem 1
Find maximal departure delay in minutes for each airline. Sort results from smallest to largest maximum delay. Output airline names and values of the delay.
SELECT a.Name AS airline_name,
       MAX(p.DepDelay) AS max_departure_delay_minutes
FROM al_perf p
JOIN L_AIRLINE_ID a ON a.ID = p.DOT_ID_Reporting_Airline
WHERE p.DepTime <> ''
GROUP BY a.ID, a.Name
ORDER BY max_departure_delay_minutes ASC;

title: SQL Questions
text:
Problem 2
Find maximal early departures in minutes for each airline. Sort results from largest to smallest. Output airline names.
An early departure has a negative DepDelay, so the earliest one is -MIN(DepDelay).
SELECT a.Name AS airline_name,
       -MIN(p.DepDelay) AS max_early_departure_minutes
FROM al_perf p
JOIN L_AIRLINE_ID a ON a.ID = p.DOT_ID_Reporting_Airline
WHERE p.DepTime <> ''
  AND p.DepDelay < 0
GROUP BY a.ID, a.Name
ORDER BY max_early_departure_minutes DESC;

title: SQL Questions
text:
Problem 3
Rank days of the week by the number of flights performed by all airlines on that day (1 is the busiest). Output the day of the week names, number of flights and ranks in the rank increasing order.
SELECT w.Day AS day_of_week,
       COUNT(*) AS num_flights,
       RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS day_rank
FROM al_perf p
JOIN L_WEEKDAYS w ON w.Code = p.DayOfWeek
GROUP BY w.Code, w.Day
ORDER BY day_rank;

title: SQL Questions
text:
Problem 4
Find the airport that has the highest average departure delay among all airports. Consider 0 minutes delay for flights that departed early. Output one line of results: the airport name, code, and average delay.
GREATEST(DepDelay, 0) counts early departures as 0 minutes.
SELECT ap.Name AS airport_name,
       p.Origin AS airport_code,
       ROUND(AVG(GREATEST(p.DepDelay, 0)), 2) AS avg_departure_delay_minutes
FROM al_perf p
JOIN L_AIRPORT ap ON ap.Code = p.Origin
WHERE p.DepTime <> ''
GROUP BY p.Origin, ap.Name
ORDER BY AVG(GREATEST(p.DepDelay, 0)) DESC
LIMIT 1;

title: SQL Questions
text:
Problem 5
For each airline find an airport where it has the highest average departure delay. Output an airline name, a name of the airport that has the highest average delay, and the value of that average delay.
The CTE gets each airline’s average delay at each airport, and RANK() keeps the top airport for each airline.
WITH airline_airport AS (
    SELECT p.DOT_ID_Reporting_Airline AS airline_id,
           p.Origin AS airport_code,
           AVG(GREATEST(p.DepDelay, 0)) AS avg_delay
    FROM al_perf p
    WHERE p.DepTime <> ''
    GROUP BY p.DOT_ID_Reporting_Airline, p.Origin
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT airline_id, airport_code, avg_delay,
           RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY airline_id ORDER BY avg_delay DESC) AS rnk
    FROM airline_airport
)
SELECT a.Name AS airline_name,
       ap.Name AS airport_name,
       ROUND(r.avg_delay, 2) AS avg_departure_delay_minutes
FROM ranked r
JOIN L_AIRLINE_ID a ON a.ID = r.airline_id
JOIN L_AIRPORT ap ON ap.Code = r.airport_code
WHERE r.rnk = 1
ORDER BY r.avg_delay DESC;

Problem 6a
Check if your dataset has any canceled flights.
SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_flights,
       SUM(Cancelled = 1) AS cancelled_flights,
       ROUND(100 * SUM(Cancelled = 1) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct_cancelled
FROM al_perf;

title: SQL Questions
text:
Problem 6b
If it does, what was the most frequent reason for each departure airport? Output airport name, the most frequent reason, and the number of cancelations for that reason.
WITH airport_reason AS (
    SELECT p.Origin AS airport_code,
           p.CancellationCode,
           COUNT(*) AS num_cancellations
    FROM al_perf p
    WHERE p.Cancelled = 1
    GROUP BY p.Origin, p.CancellationCode
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT airport_code, CancellationCode, num_cancellations,
           RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY airport_code ORDER BY num_cancellations DESC) AS rnk
    FROM airport_reason
)
SELECT ap.Name AS airport_name,
       c.Reason AS most_frequent_reason,
       r.num_cancellations
FROM ranked r
JOIN L_AIRPORT ap ON ap.Code = r.airport_code
JOIN L_CANCELATION c ON c.Code = r.CancellationCode
WHERE r.rnk = 1
ORDER BY r.num_cancellations DESC, airport_name, most_frequent_reason;
